zebralogic.title: RelativeOrdering
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says X is somewhere to the left (or right) of Y, enforce that X's house index is less (or greater) than Y's index.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue uses phrases like "somewhere to the left of", "to the right of", "left of", or "right of" without specifying adjacency.
zebralogic.example: The model placed X to the right of Y even though the clue said X is somewhere to the left of Y.

zebralogic.title: EquivalenceLinking
zebralogic.principle: When a clue equates two attribute values (e.g., "the associate degree holder owns the Toyota Camry"), assign them to the same house.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue contains an equality or "is the same as" relationship between two attributes.
zebralogic.example: The model treated "X is the same as Y" as unrelated, assigning them to different houses.

zebralogic.title: FixedHouseAssignment
zebralogic.principle: If a clue fixes an attribute to a specific house number, enforce that exact placement as a hard constraint.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue mentions a specific house number (e.g., "the first house", "house 3") for an attribute.
zebralogic.example: The model ignored a clue that fixed a specific attribute to house 3, placing it elsewhere.

zebralogic.title: CompactFinalAnswer
zebralogic.principle: The solution JSON must be the very last part of the response with no extra characters after it; otherwise the verifier may miss the answer.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: At the end of generation, ensure only the JSON is output and stop immediately after it.
zebralogic.example: The model placed the solution JSON before the end of the response or added extra commentary after it, causing the verifier to miss the answer.

zebralogic.title: NegativeHouseAssignment
zebralogic.principle: When a clue explicitly forbids an attribute from being in a particular house, enforce that the attribute cannot be placed there.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue contains "not in house X", "doesn't live in the third house", etc.
zebralogic.example: The model placed an attribute in a house that a clue explicitly forbids.

zebralogic.title: TransitiveEquivalencePropagation
zebralogic.principle: When multiple equivalence clues form a chain (A = B and B = C), propagate the equivalence so all involved attributes are assigned to the same house.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When there are two or more equality clues linking a series of attributes.
zebralogic.example: The model failed to propagate a chain of equivalences, leaving two linked attributes in different houses.

zebralogic.title: ExactAttributeValueMatching
zebralogic.principle: Copy attribute values exactly as they appear in the problem statement, preserving spelling, case, and punctuation.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When writing the final solution, ensure each attribute value matches the original text.
zebralogic.example: The model misspelled an attribute value, e.g., "desert" as "dessert".

zebralogic.title: LimitReasoningLength
zebralogic.principle: Keep reasoning concise enough to stay within the model's token budget; avoid overly verbose explanations that may be truncated.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: During the reasoning phase, limit the amount of text to avoid exceeding token limits.
zebralogic.example: The model's reasoning was too verbose, causing the verifier to truncate the answer.

zebralogic.title: ChildRelationshipParsing
zebralogic.principle: When a clue refers to a person as the mother/father of X, interpret it as linking the child attribute rather than a simple equivalence.
zebralogic.example: The model misinterpreted a clue like "Bob is the father of Alice" as a simple equivalence rather than linking a child relationship.

zebralogic.title: ExactDistanceConstraint
zebralogic.principle: When a clue specifies that there is exactly N houses between X and Y (including directly adjacent when N=0), enforce that the absolute difference in house indices equals N+1; this also covers "directly left/right of" and "next to".
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue contains phrases like "there is N house(s) between X and Y", "directly left of", "directly right of", or "next to".
zebralogic.example: The clue says "There is one house between X and Y" but the model placed X and Y adjacent, treating the distance incorrectly.

zebralogic.description: Misinterpreting 'N houses between' as 'N houses apart'
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model often treats the phrase "N houses between" as meaning the two houses are N positions apart, forgetting that there must be N houses in between, which adds one extra house to the distance.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Explicitly convert "N houses between X and Y" to the constraint |pos(X) - pos(Y)| = N + 1; double‑check the distance calculation.

zebralogic.description: Placing the solution JSON before the end of the response or adding excessive text after it, causing the verifier to miss the answer
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model may continue to generate commentary after the JSON, or insert the JSON earlier, due to lack of a clear stopping condition.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Generate the JSON as the final output and stop generation immediately after it; avoid any trailing characters.

zebralogic.description: Exceeding token limit causing the verifier to truncate
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model includes too much reasoning or repeats information, exceeding the allowed token budget, leading to truncation of the answer.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Keep reasoning concise, prioritize essential deductions, and stop before reaching the token limit.

zebralogic.description: Ignoring negative house constraints (placing an attribute in a house that a clue explicitly forbids)
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model may focus on positive constraints and overlook constraints that forbid placements.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Treat negative clues as hard constraints that eliminate possible house positions for the mentioned attribute.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model may forget to output the solution JSON entirely, perhaps due to an early termination or oversight.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Ensure that the final step always includes the solution JSON in the required format.
